## Context
Linear OAuth, connection persistence, and webhook delivery storage are now live in auth-broker. The broker currently exposes `/v1/auth/linear/connections` and `/v1/auth/linear/deliveries*` without a real authenticated user/team access model.

## Goals
- Define and implement the auth model for broker-side Linear routes.
- Scope connection and delivery visibility by Better Auth user and org/team membership.
- Prevent unauthenticated listing or mutation of connected account metadata and pending webhook deliveries.

## Notes
- Current provider metadata explicitly reports `accessControlMode: manual_unenforced`.
- Linear callback now links Better Auth users by email and persists `betterAuthUserId`, so the next step is enforcement, not more identity capture.
- Consider whether local clients should use Better Auth sessions, broker-issued device claims, or signed service tokens.

## Links
- services/auth-broker/src/modules/linear-connections/plugin.ts
- services/auth-broker/src/modules/linear-sync-store/plugin.ts

## Context
Linear OAuth, connection persistence, pending webhook deliveries, and Better Auth user/org scoping are now live in `auth-broker`, and unauthenticated access to connection/delivery routes is blocked.

## Goals
- Finish the remaining access-control work by enforcing team-scoped visibility and mutation rules for Linear connection and delivery routes.
- Preserve legacy fallback behavior for user-owned and org-owned records created before team ownership is first-class.
- Make provider/access metadata accurately report the strongest active Better Auth scope.

## Notes
- This ticket now covers the remaining team-authz gap only; user/org scoping is already shipped.
- Depends on first-class ownership persistence so team ownership is queryable without JSON-envelope fallbacks.

## Context
Hack should support multiple login methods for the same Better Auth user without fragmenting identity. GitHub social login is wired today; Google is not yet wired in this broker.

## Goals
- Enable strict verified-email account linking across login methods.
- Keep GitHub-as-login separate from GitHub-as-integration.
- Add Google Better Auth provider support behind env-driven config if credentials are present.
- Ensure mismatched or unverified emails never auto-link.

## Notes
- Account linking must only happen for verified matching email, not raw email string equality alone.
- This is about Hack login methods, not provider integration profiles.

## Context
Broker-owned auth and provider ownership make it practical to move beyond machine-local keychain-only storage for some project-scoped encrypted env/secret use cases. We need a deliberate design before implementing any remote secret portability.

## Goals
- Design a per-project encrypted env/secret portability model owned by Hack user/org/team.
- Evaluate project keys or envelope-encryption approaches for cross-machine and remote-node portability.
- Define trust boundaries between local keychain custody, broker-owned metadata, and decrypt-capable clients.
- Keep local-only secret workflows viable.

## Notes
- This is a design/spec ticket, not immediate implementation work.
- It should connect to future remote node portability work and reduce single-machine lock-in without weakening the security model.

## Links
- docs/plans/2026-03-06-hack-account-auth-and-provider-ux-design.md
- T-00180

## Context
T-00194 defines the design boundary for portable remote encrypted project env storage under Hack account ownership. The next execution slice should implement only the default remote bundle registry plus explicit CLI publish/fetch/apply flows.

## Goals
- Add broker-owned encrypted env bundle storage and project binding records.
- Add Better Auth-gated broker routes for publish/list/fetch/bind operations.
- Add CLI commands for explicit publish, pull, apply, and binding management.
- Keep local `.hack/.env` as the default path.

## Notes
- This is the first implementation slice from `docs/plans/2026-03-06-remote-encrypted-project-env-portability-plan.md`.
- Out of scope: automatic remote-node hydration, sharing UX, recovery, rotation, provider-token portability.
- Prefer a single default remote bundle binding per project in this phase.

## Context
Broker-owned auth and provider ownership make it practical to move beyond machine-local keychain-only storage for some project-scoped encrypted env and secret use cases. This ticket is the design/spec boundary for portable remote encrypted project env storage under Hack account ownership.

## Goals
- Define ownership, encryption, storage, trust boundaries, and rollout phases for portable project env bundles.
- Keep local-only env workflows viable and unchanged by default.
- Make the next implementation slice concrete without pulling it into the current provider/auth implementation pass.

## Notes
- Design and phased execution plan are now captured in `docs/plans/2026-03-06-remote-encrypted-project-env-portability-plan.md`.
- The next execution ticket is `T-00195` and is intentionally limited to the phase-1 broker and CLI slice.
- Out of scope for the current pass: remote-node hydration, sharing UX, recovery, rotation, provider-token portability.
- Phase 1 should ship a single default remote bundle binding per project before any named multi-bundle model.

## Links

## Context
Hack now has several fundamental product-level changes: Hack account auth, broker-owned provider connections, Linear sync, remote node routing, and upcoming shared remote features. Today those changes are discoverable only through release notes, appcast text, or direct documentation.

## Goals
- Add a first-class "What's New" / release announcement surface for Hack Desktop.
- Add a CLI-facing release summary path so major changes are discoverable outside the macOS app.
- Define how GitHub releases, appcast notes, and in-product announcement content are generated from a single source.
- Keep the presentation concise and version-aware instead of banner-heavy.

## Notes
- Prefer one source of truth that can render to Sparkle/appcast notes, GitHub Releases, and in-app/in-CLI announcement surfaces.
- Include a way to spotlight changes that alter auth or provider setup requirements.
- Consider a dismissible per-version experience in the app and a lightweight CLI command such as `hack whats-new`.

## Links

- apps/macos/Packages/Features/DashboardFeature
